question: Should OpenClaw pursue a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract in core/plugin APIs, document Redis/BullMQ-style orchestration as external/plugin-only, or defer this until the narrower HA/runtime/session trackers settle?
rationale: The issue is not a small bug fix; it requires product and architecture intent across core leanness, plugin seams, config surface, backend dependencies, security posture, and deployment topology.

options.title: Design backend-neutral contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broad architecture tracker and first specify scheduler ownership, job claiming, retries, observability, config, and plugin/backend boundaries before choosing Redis/BullMQ or another backend.

options.title: Route to external/plugin-only prototype
options.body: Treat ScalyClaw and similar implementations as external prior art and only add OpenClaw API seams if the prototype proves a missing core contract.

options.title: Defer behind narrower trackers
options.body: Pause broad horizontal-scaling work until cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, and worker-auth decisions each settle.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broad architecture tracker and first specify scheduler ownership, job claiming, retries, observability, config, and plugin/backend boundaries before choosing Redis/BullMQ or another backend.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the maintainer-facing keep-open architecture signal and is tied to the relevant queue/cron product boundary history.
